analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md, lines 676-684 on the head side. It replaces the description of how a stop is propagated during cluster start. Previously the joined Mac inferred a stop after the leader's status stayed 'Stopped' for 20 seconds. Now the leader counts each stop request and carries the count in its status. The joined Mac ends its follow immediately when the count changes, and a 'Stopped' status alone no longer counts as a stop.

This is documentation only. No code, authorization, attestation, encryption, App Attest grant, or coordinator behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The text describes cluster stop/restart control over the cable, which is an operator-driven local availability control. It does not touch the TB-011 serving authorization or its replay, revocation and binding (T-053), the TB-012 add-on hold socket (T-059/T-060), or the cache threat T-041.

Open question for later passes that have the code: the stop counter is carried in the leader's cable status. Whether that status is authenticated to the paired peer is unverified here. A forged or replayed count could end the other Mac's follow, which would be an availability issue only. The counter implementation is not supplied, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding. The remaining unchanged document text is orientation context only. No new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption is visible from the doc edit.
